verdict_vs_market.quote: This is a solid, market-level Google L6 offer—not an exceptional one.

verdict_vs_current.quote: The missing input is your forward-looking Meta compensation, not your trailing W-2.

recommendation.quote: Negotiate—do not accept the first offer and do not walk away yet.

equity_grounding.quote: That is an aggressive but defensible anchor: approximately the upper end of reported L6 PM compensation

uses_public_incumbent_benchmark.quote: Current compensation reporting puts Google L6 Senior PM median compensation around $551K in the Bay Area.

refresh_valued_at.quote: Value refreshers at zero in your baseline calculation. Treat them as potential upside.

up_level_ask.quote: Whether there is any flexibility on level if your Meta scope is demonstrably above Google L6 scope.

level_claim.quote: You are happy, the Google move is essentially lateral

walkaway_tied_to.quote: Accept only if the revised package beats your forward-looking Meta compensation by roughly 10%–15%

unsupported_claims.claim: Google uses a front-loaded 38/32/20/10 vesting schedule for new hires
unsupported_claims.quote: Google’s current new-hire schedule is commonly reported as 38% / 32% / 20% / 10%, rather than 25% each year.

unsupported_claims.claim: Equity has more negotiating flexibility than base salary at Google
unsupported_claims.quote: Base is valuable because it recurs and drives the bonus, but equity often has more negotiating flexibility.

missing_info_requested: Exact RSU vesting schedule and cadence
Forfeited Meta equity and bonus amounts

specific_ask_without_gap.quote: Ask for: - Base: $260,000 - New-hire RSUs: $1,400,000 - Sign-on bonus: $100,000

year1_vs_recurring.quote: Base is valuable because it recurs and drives the bonus, but equity often has more negotiating flexibility. A sign-on is especially important

forfeiture_as_loss.quote: Separately ask Google to make you whole for near-term Meta compensation you lose by resigning.
